descs.t: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate race, and appeared with him at a Detroit church days before Tuesday's vote. She lost the primary to El-Sayed with 47.55% and first endorsed him. We go through what she said, how both campaigns reacted, and what the polls show.

Haley Stevens crossed party lines to back Mike Rogers for the Michigan Senate seat, saying she cannot stand with hate. Democrats from Michigan to Washington are calling it betrayal, while El-Sayed's campaign says it raised $1.2 million in four hours. We look at why she did it and whether it changes Tuesday's result.

A Democrat who lost the Michigan primary to Abdul El-Sayed now says her vote goes to Republican Mike Rogers, and she said it standing beside him: we cannot stand with hate. Her own party is in revolt and Trump says he would love to have her. We break down the fallout and what it means for the fight for the Senate.

intro.plain: Big turn in Michigan. Democrat Haley Stevens, who lost the Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, just endorsed the Republican, Mike Rogers, and stood next to him at a Detroit church. Her party is furious, Trump is praising her, and the vote is Tuesday. So tell me in the chat: does an endorsement like this move any votes at all?
intro.mid: Haley Stevens just did what almost no Democrat does: she endorsed the Republican in a Senate race days before the vote. Her reason, in her words, we cannot stand with hate. El-Sayed's camp says it raised $1.2 million in four hours off the back of it. Chat, is this principle or payback for a lost primary?
intro.bold: A Democrat just stood next to Mike Rogers and said her vote goes to him, not to her own party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. We cannot stand with hate, she said. Her party is calling her a traitor and Trump wants her in the GOP. So I want to hear it from you in the chat: betrayal, or the bravest move of the cycle?

hook.plain: A Democrat who lost the Michigan primary just endorsed the Republican, days before the vote. Here is what she said and why her party is in uproar.
hook.mid: She endorsed him after the primary. Now she stands next to his Republican rival. Here is why Haley Stevens switched, and what it could do on Tuesday.
hook.bold: We cannot stand with hate. That is how Haley Stevens explained backing a Republican over her own party's nominee. Here is the fallout.

descs.t: Texas early voting closed with 7,705,786 votes, about 74.1% of projected final turnout, ahead of Tuesday's Senate race between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico. Recent polls range from Paxton ahead by 0.6 to Talarico ahead by 4. We go through the numbers and what they can and cannot tell us.

With 7.7 million early votes in, Texas heads into Tuesday with a Senate race the polls cannot agree on: Trafalgar has Ken Paxton up 0.6, YouGov has James Talarico up 4. The governor's race between Greg Abbott and Gina Hinojosa also looks close in some polls. We look at where Texas really stands.

Texas turned out in near presidential numbers before Election Day, and Ken Paxton's Senate race against James Talarico is within a point in one final poll. Democrats talk about flipping the state, Republicans say Latino men are sticking with Trump. We break down the early vote and what it means for Tuesday.

intro.plain: Texas early voting is done: 7,705,786 votes, about 74.1% of the projected turnout. The Senate race is Ken Paxton against James Talarico, and the final polls disagree, from Paxton up 0.6 to Talarico up 4. Chat, if you are in Texas, did you vote early, and how does it feel on the ground?
intro.mid: Texas just finished early voting with 7.7 million ballots. One final poll has Ken Paxton ahead by 0.6, another has James Talarico ahead by 4. The governor's race may be close too. That is not the Texas we are used to. Chat, is this the year Texas surprises everyone, or is it hype?
intro.bold: Texas turned out in force: 7.7 million early votes, and Ken Paxton's Senate race is within a point in one final poll. Democrats think they can flip it, Republicans say the base is holding. Two days out, Texas is a real fight. So chat, call it now: Paxton or Talarico?

Axios also reports Netanyahu is pressing for a strike right after Tuesday's midterm elections. We go through what was reported and what is only claimed.

Axios says Netanyahu is pressing Trump to strike the Islamic Republic immediately after the midterms, while Tucker Carlson claims a nuclear strike could be days away. Trump calls the call good. We separate the reporting from the claims and look at what each side wants next.

Netanyahu wants the regime hit as soon as Tuesday's vote is done, according to Axios, and Trump says the two had a good conversation about it. Tucker Carlson is warning of a nuclear strike, and critics call that a hoax. We cut through the noise and lay out what pressure on the Islamic Republic looks like now.

descs.t: A federal judge in Alaska has dismissed the Trump administration's lawsuit over two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the Senate ballot, a suit that sought to stop certification if Democrat Mary Peltola wins. The Justice Department says it will appeal. We go through what the case claimed and what the ruling means.

The Justice Department lost its bid to hold up Alaska's Senate certification over the so called Decoy Dan, a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot. Reports say it will appeal, and Trump is pushing back on calls that the case was meritless. We look at the ruling and the race it hangs over.

A federal judge just threw out the DOJ's attempt to stall Alaska's Senate result if Mary Peltola beats GOP Senator Dan Sullivan. Trump asks what is meritless, and an appeal is promised. We lay out the fight and what it could mean for control of the Senate.

intro.plain: In Alaska, a federal judge has dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit over two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the Senate ballot. The suit wanted certification held up if Democrat Mary Peltola wins. The department says it will appeal. Chat, does a second candidate with the same name confuse voters, or is this a fight over nothing?
intro.mid: The Trump Justice Department just lost in court in Alaska. It sued over a second Dan Sullivan on the Senate ballot and wanted certification stopped if Mary Peltola wins. The judge dismissed it, and the department says it will appeal. Chat, is this a real ballot problem or a legal Hail Mary?

With the Senate on the line Tuesday, this matters. Chat, should a court ever hold up a count over a name on the ballot?
